utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, I told you I wanted to turn to the question of the circumstances that existed at the time and that were part of the decisions being made about mobilisation and recruitment at that time. First of all, this was all taking place in the context of both the discussions of independence concerning Croatia and Slovenia and the concern about imminent conflict in both of those republics. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that changes to the military service law were carried out in 1990. I did not deal with political with issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm going to tell you then that at this time many people were aware of the fact that Croatia and Slovenia were threatening to leave former Yugoslavia and that there was great concern about conflict between the JNA and those republics, among many of the people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Did that escape your attention?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was also concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There were also concerns among many people in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in other republics about new recruits, that is young recruits, not reservists, being sent outside of their republics to fight in either Slovenia or Croatia. Isn't that also correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that is so. I was not conducting the policy of the Yugoslav People's Army, nor did I monitor activities in the JNA or the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, it's odd that you say you don't know about that, because I could have sworn that yesterday I heard you mention a conversation with Minister Doko where he spoke about demonstrations and protests to you. I didn't realise as you were giving your testimony that you had no idea what Minister Doko was talking about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you what he talked about. He mentioned the protests of mothers who did not want to have recruits sent to serve their military term, and he asked me -- I already said that. I don't want to repeat it. If you wish, I can explain who these mothers were who were protesting in front of the building. This is information from the Bosnia and Herzegovina state security. None of them had a son in the army or even had a male child to send to the JNA; they were paid. They were doing this for money, which was also offered to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, is that your perception of what was happening in July and August of 1991, that not one parent whose mobilisation or recruitment-eligible child was at risk of being sent to fight in another republic in a clash they disagreed with protested or demonstrated against it? That everybody who participated in the demonstration was a fraud who was paid? Is that essentially your perception of what was going on at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not how I see things. Many parents were concerned; quite rightly so. All I said was that information about the mothers who were protesting publicly in front of the National Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina -- actually, that information that I mentioned just now is not something that comes from me, but it's the information that comes from the Bosnia and Herzegovina state security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's not quibble about that, Mr. Kapetina. The fact is that part of the context is that many people were concerned that protests were happening. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time there were no mass protests.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in addition there had been a conference at Brioni in which -- and at least an agreement in principle was reached concerning the threatened conflicts. And that was another factor that was cited by the Bosnian government in its decisions about whether or not mobilisation and recruitment should be implemented on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite clear, at that time there was no mobilisation being carried out on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because serving one's military term of duty does not mean being mobilised. Right now I don't know what kind of meeting was held at Brioni or the outcome or the agreements stemming from that meeting. Probably at the time I did know, but right now I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, you are also aware that the Bosnian government asserted that the mobilisation was unlawful for a number of reasons, including the fact that it was not legitimately directed at determining combat-readiness and including the fact that it had not been ordered by the SFRY Presidency. You knew that at the time, didn't you? That was part of this ongoing discussion and dispute.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not implementing policy at the defence of ministry -- the defence ministry; I was implementing laws. If something was agreed on the political side, then they should have informed the government and all the relevant departments, as you say, to selectively apply the law, what should have been done and what should not have been done. But this kind of information was not something that we had access to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, the whole public had access to it because this was being written about in the media. It's of great interest to the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina and newspapers were writing about it. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that the whole media wrote about it. I was not obliged to listen to the media or the public in my job; I was obliged to implement laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, I'm not suggesting to you that the whole media was writing about it; that's a characterisation I think you put on it. What I am suggesting to you is that enough of the media was writing about it so that you were very much aware of it at the time. And those are all factors you chose to ignore in painting a very misleading picture to the Court about what was happening at that time. Now, let me address just a couple more issues. First of all, did you know at the time who the prime minister of the federal government was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did you know that the Federal Executive Council in early August took the position that TO units were being engaged in certain parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina arbitrarily and outside the authorities of the republic and the federation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not duty-bound to implement decisions of the Federal Executive Council. That's what the inspections at the federal ministry of defence at the Yugoslav level was supposed to do. So that's why we did not do that. You said just now that that was a question of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, no one asked you whether you were duty-bound to implement the decisions of the Federal Executive Council. The question was whether you were aware of the position explained by Mr. Tieger taken by that council. So please concentrate on the questions. Let me give you another example where you really tend to, at least confuse me. A little bit earlier you were asked about whether many people in Bosnia were concerned about young recruits, et cetera, and then you said you don't know if that's -- and some 20 lines later you say: Parents were concerned, and rightly so. So do you understand that it's -- could confuse me if you on the one hand say: Well, I don't know; and the other hand, 20 lines later say: Yes, parents were rightly concerned about this situation? And here again you're responding to a question which is not put to you. You don't have to defend yourself here from knowing what -- you're just asked to tell us what you know. It may be that you knew about it, that you felt no responsibility, or that you even strongly disagreed with the position, and perhaps rightly so. I don't know. But please concentrate on what is asked and answer those questions. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn to tab 37 of the Prosecution binder, and can that be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 37, Your Honours, will be P1037.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kapetina, I want to direct your attention to two portions of tab 37 which contains an article by -- an article of -- an issue, excuse me, of Oslobodjenje in July 1991. And first I want to turn your attention to the reproduction of the letter of the BH Presidency to the Federal Executive Board on the mobilisation in Bosnian Krajina listing eight reasons against, I think is part of the heading. Do you see that portion of the issue? Now, in it a number of reasons are listed by the BH Presidency for ending the mobilisation effort, and those include the following: That the mobilisation was not ordered by the SFRY Presidency; that the mobilisation obviously does not aim to check combat-readiness; is that the BH authorities were not informed of it happening in a timely fashion; that it has harmful political consequences and contributes to the deterioration of inter-ethnic relations; creates or deepens mistrust for the JNA; it's in contradiction of the provisions of the OEBS; it's in contradiction with the declaration adopted during talks with the representatives in Brioni; and it causes great financial expense and is not in compliance with the present financial situation. Did those reasons, whether you agree with them or not, given by the -- publicised by the Bosnian government escape your attention in 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't informed about this letter that was sent probably to the SFRY Presidency, but from this attachment here I cannot really read anything here in this title, eight reasons. It's so small, the print is so small, that I really cannot -- but very well. You've told me all the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm going to intercede. If he can't read them, then my learned friend should put them to him one by one because he can't be expected to remember all eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just listed those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue is not whether he remembers all of these reasons. The clear issue is the following: Mr. Tieger asked you whether it escaped your attention that it was published that the Federal - what was it? - Executive Council, I think, took strong position, whether it's 8 or 7 or 6, were you aware of such a position taken by this body, or were you aware of a publication in which this is referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've said before that it wasn't my job to cover the Yugoslav People's Army and the Territorial Defence. This information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not ask you whether it was your job. I didn't ask you whether you were informed about it. Did you, at that time, learn about it, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was following all the events, and I cannot tell you anything specific about whether I knew something at the time or not. But I was following all of the political and social events. It's hard after 15 years to say now whether I knew that at the time or not. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, it was an issue which, in view of your letter, the legality of this activity was one of the subjects that was of interest to you, wasn't it? I mean, that's how I understood your concerns about illegal activity, that this was something you were very much interested in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just said that. I really cannot talk about individual meetings, conclusions, or decisions of the federal organs. I probably did follow all of those things, but I cannot give you a certain answer about that particular piece of information and the eight conditions. The Presidency probably gave other conditions and sought other agreements which were not respected. I didn't point to them because I didn't think that they were relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is at least an answer to the question which was put in different ways several times to you. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Two matters before we break. The same issue of Oslobodjenje indicates -- reports something from the Tanjug, I believe, from July 12th, that is that: "At today's meeting the Federal Executive Council discussed the situation in the country and the measures to halt armed conflicts, which is in the country's essential interest, the Federal Executive Council also estimates that TO units are being engaged in certain parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina arbitrarily and outside the areas of the republic and the federation." The Federal Executive Council, Mr. Kapetina, was headed by Ante Markovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me also quickly ask you to turn to tab 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I would ask that that be given a number as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, 26 would be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1038, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: P1038, tab 26, contains the recording, the transcript recording, of a news conference held by Stipe Mesic, who at that time was the president of the SFRY and Presidency. Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in the first paragraph in which he speaks, Mr. Mesic says: "As far as the mobilisation is concerned, you know that the Presidency was not constituted, in other words, the supreme command was not functioning, and that what was done was done outside the supreme command." So were you also aware at the time of the events we've been discussing that the president of the Presidency, Stipe Mesic, also asserted that the -- as did the Bosnian government, that the mobilisation was outside the -- was done outside the proper channels?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. What's given to me here is just a statement by one of the members of the Presidency, Mr. Mesic. Does that necessarily mean that it's true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked whether you know about it. The answer is no, yes? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you aware or unaware that there was at least a debate or dispute or conflict about the legality and propriety and potential consequences of the mobilisation and recruitment efforts during that period of time and at the time you wrote your warning letter? Whether you're aware of these specifics, all the specifics we just discussed, were you aware of the dispute and debate generally?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware that there was a general debate. If you are using newspaper articles for that, I must say that Oslobodjenje at the time was quite partial as well as other media. There was a general propaganda campaign so that the writing of the media in this case doesn't mean much. I can remind you of another statement of Mr. Mesic when he completed his term of office when he said: I have completed my task. Yugoslavia is no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you again. If you say: Oslobodjenje at that time was quite partial, did you read these reports, whether true or not, in Oslobodjenje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So do I understand your testimony to be that you were aware that for good reasons or perfectly wrong reasons, that the issue was raised in the media, the issue of the legality of this recruitment and the matters we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those issues should be discussed in the institutions of the system and not in the public or in the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you what should have been done. I asked you whether I understood your testimony well, that for good or bad reasons that the issue was raised in the media. Even if you consider that to be a totally wrong thing to do, were you aware of the matter being raised in the media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the topical matters were also covered by the media, so that question was probably covered, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Probably? Was it covered, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That question did figure, to an extent, in the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Tieger, I think it's time for a break. We're late already. We'll have a break of 20 minutes until quarter past 6.00. And, Mr. Kapetina, may I really urge you again to answer to the questions. This is not a place to -- I'm not saying that what you want to tell us is not important and is not true, but it's very often not an answer to the question. And I urge you again, because I think you came here to testify, you were requested to testify by the Defence in this case, and if you do not answer the questions that might -- might, to some extent, invalidate your own testimony because the Chamber does not hear what you know about the matters you were asked about, if you again and again turn away from the questions. We stand adjourned until quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I ask the Witness and the Court to turn to tab 4, and may that item be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 4, Your Honours, will be P1039.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, I see you have been looking over P1039 while the logistical procedure has been implemented. That's a conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Simovic on August 27th, 1991. And as you may already have seen on the first page Mr. Simovic advises Dr. Karadzic that he wants to inform him briefly about a letter by our chief inspector warning about unlawful acts. As we continue on to page 2 after a brief discussion about a second issue, Dr. Karadzic says: "This thing with the inspector is certain. Everybody should do his own job, and we'll see who in the end will be responsible." Mr. Simovic -- and Dr. Karadzic continues. "But I want to move through this quickly."

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMOVIC SAYS
utterances.text: "That's the best. We have officially addressed the president of the Presidency, president of the government, president of the Assembly, and the press, at the government session, 15 minutes in detail."

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC ASKS
utterances.text: "Who is the inspector?"

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMOVIC SAYS
utterances.text: "Our guy, Kapetina."

utterances.speaker: DR. KARADZIC SAYS
utterances.text: "I see." And Mr. Simovic says: "We have activated him. He does his part of work fully. Doko is almost seeking his life. However, we shall protect him. He is doing what he is supposed to do in accordance with law." And Dr. Karadzic says: "Yes, yes, good, good." I had asked you earlier, Mr. Kapetina, about whether or not you had been activated by the SDS, whether or not you had been doing your part of work for the SDS, and let me ask you again if Mr. Simovic's remarks to Dr. Karadzic reflect the fact that at that point and thereafter, you were pursuing tasks for the SDS of various sorts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. I wasn't activated by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, we're -- again, I noticed before we had some smallish debates, if you will, about the nuances of questions. So let me -- let's not get hung up on the meaning of "activate" or "not activate." Let me simply ask you if at this point and thereafter you were given tasks by the SDS and performed those tasks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't assigned tasks, not then, not to the end of 1991 or the end of 1992 -- or rather, while I worked in the ministry I received not one single task from the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me turn next to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I don't think it really assists the Chamber very much to hear whether the witness received a task from the SDS, not having identified what you consider to be the SDS. Would that be SDS officials? Would that be SDS party organs? But perhaps I put it to you, Mr. Kapetina. You were just asked about whether you received tasks from the SDS. You said: "No, I never did receive tasks, I never performed tasks." Would that include -- well, let's say, SDS members with important positions or SDS organs because it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It would refer to both individuals and SDS organs. I didn't receive tasks from anybody, and by the same token, I didn't carry any tasks out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have one other question for you. It seems on the basis of this intercept that Mr. Simovic has a rather different perception of the interactions you had. You said: "I consulted him once on that letter I intended to write," whereas Mr. Simovic seems to have a totally different impression. Do you have any explanation for the difference of perception of what happened at that time between you and Mr. Simovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know what you're referring to when you said that Simovic seems to have different views.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it seems that Mr. Simovic, at least if we read the intercept, "I will want to inform you briefly. I will send you a letter by our chief inspector warning about unlawful acts." And Mr. Simovic calls you "our guy." Mr. Simovic says: "We have activated him. He does his part of work fully." Would you agree with me that that's at least a different perception from the interaction you had with him, if we compare it to your perception, just having consulted him once to seek protection? You say: "He couldn't tell me that he would protect me." Mr. Simovic saying: "We shall protect him." I mean, it's a totally different story, the story you tell us and the story Mr. Simovic seems to present in this telephone conversation to Mr. Karadzic. So therefore my question is: Do you have any explanation for that? Could you know -- do you know any reason for such a difference in perception?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't wish to enter into the opinion presented by Mr. Simovic in his conversation with Mr. Karadzic, but Miodrag Simovic told me that the government can relieve me of my duties and that they could not protect me because they would be outvoted at the government meeting. That's the point. Now, how else could he protect me? I don't know, and I didn't ask him to do so either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I do understand that you have no explanation, apart from drawing our attention to the illogic statement that he could protect you. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to add something, please, Your Honour? Miodrag Simovic was the vice-premier of the government, and to all intents and purposes he refers to all the cadres in the government as "ours" because he's speaking on behalf of the government. So that's the jargon. He says "ours," "our guy," because everybody in the government is his -- an employee of his, a worker of his, and that's the jargon he uses in his conversation. But I don't belong to anybody nor can anybody appropriate me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's turn to tab 6, please, and I'd like that given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1040, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, for practical reasons if a number is asked, if I do not object against it, then you may immediately give a number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, P1040 are notes from the meeting of officials and top-ranking personnel of republican state organs, members of the SDS, Bosnia-Herzegovina dated September 12th, 1991, notes from that meeting. And if we turn to page 4 of the English, item number 11, the notes indicate the following: "Propose the establishment of a system of duty shifts to monitor the activities and execution of tasks in the operations of state organs. Resolution of existing problems in the various fields and maintaining contacts with the SDS. Ljubisav Terzic and Dragan Kapetina are entrusted with this and a development of means of communication between SDS and SDS personnel in republican state organs with the municipalities." Mr. Kapetina, isn't this one of the reflections of Mr. Simovic's indications to Dr. Karadzic, that you would be -- that you were working well for SDS, that you had been activated and would be performing tasks? Isn't this one of the tasks that you were given and undertook?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Do you wish further explanation? At the meeting I most probably was not present myself. Perhaps the first man there, Ljubisav Terzic, might have attended that meeting who was appointed by the Serbian Democratic Party as vice-secretary in the ministry. Now, the fact that somebody had put me in there, perhaps they did because they knew that I could -- that I was capable of doing that kind of work, that kind of job.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So what does that mean --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about being entrusted with anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have no recollection of ever being entrusted with this assignment or any similar kind of assignment, one that relied upon your expertise and that was given to you by SDS officials or SDS members or important people who were affiliated with SDS in pursuit of basic Bosnian Serb and SDS objectives? Any recollection of anything like that, type of thing that Mr. Simovic had been referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I don't know anything about who followed SDS objectives. I can't recognise somebody as being a person following SDS objectives. And another thing, at that point in time the SDS, for me, was a political party just like any other political party in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Let me inform you that the vice-premier at each meeting held talks with Muslim cadres in the Assembly, Mr. Cengic that is, from the very first day, and I had nothing against that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You know very well that is not the issue here, Mr. Kapetina. The issue is whether or not you were somebody who was working --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the witness has answered the question. He has said that he did not know about it, that he was never tasked with this. If we look at the language, then we see that the following conclusions were drawn and then quite some activities are mentioned, facilitate, prepare, facilitate, and a couple of times we find the word "propose." And sometimes who is proposed to do this -- proposed that the SDS or proposed to the SDS, and here it just says "proposed." The witness has answered the question by saying that it never reached him. Let's please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's turn next then to an item already in evidence, and that's the stenographic record of the third session of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina held on December 11th, 1991. I don't know if that's been distributed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that under ... Mr. Tieger, could you further provide the witness where to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First at this third session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly we see at pages 29 to 30 of the English and pages 47 through 48, I believe, of the B/C/S, Mr. Krajisnik calls for the reports of the presidents of the commissions and other working bodies on the discharge of duties and tasks. And he indicates at page 31 of the English the order in which the relevant speakers will address the Assembly, beginning with Mr. Miskin, and then followed by Mr. Skoko, and ending with Mr. Mikic, and then yourself, Dragan Kapetina. Just moving through that very quickly, we see at page 32 of the English, which is approximately page 56 of the B/C/S -- excuse me, approximately page 54 of the B/C/S, Mr. Miskin discusses regionalisation, that is if Bosnia and Herzegovina were to be divided into regions and if it were to cease to exist as a single republic, the autonomous regions would comprise the territories. And he calls on page 34 of the English for an election of the council of ministers as soon as possible to carry out the activities. On pages 48 through 49 of the English -- and excuse me, let me also note page 45 of the English by Mr. Miskin, which is page 57 of the B/C/S, he notes: "Given the conditions of war in the country and the very precarious situation in BiH" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the B/C/S you said "page 57," seems not to be reproduced. There is more general terms, Mr. Tieger, only portions are reproduced in B/C/S, whereas the whole seems to be tendered in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, if I may, Your Honour, let me quickly complete that citation. It's, I believe, the comments by the witness are duplicated in full. These are -- provide the appropriate context, I think, for the Court. If it turns out, in fact, that the witness has -- was present at the meeting, has any particular concerns about the portion cited of other speakers, we can certainly find them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, whenever you want to confront the witness with certain portions of this document, he should at least have an opportunity to read the relevant portion of it. And I noticed that 57 is not among the B/C/S portions, unless you very slowly read the whole of the passage that you would like to confront him with, and even then it's not how it should be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. You're -- I agree, Your Honour, and I had intended for that passage to be duplicated in B/C/S, and I apologise both to the Court and the witness for that oversight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But I, as indicated, I think we can manage in the fashion the Court just described.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just to complete that comment by Mr. Miskin, it was: "Given the conditions of war in the country and the very precarious situation in BiH" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist me. Where are we exactly now in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Page 35, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 35, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: "We believe that in all the regions and in the entire BH, detailed contingency plans should be elaborated in the event" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not found it yet. Could you guide us to the relevant paragraph or the relevant ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm not surprised that the Court couldn't find it, and again I'm obliged to apologise to the Court. That is on page 36 in approximately the very middle. That would be about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. "Given the conditions ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. "Given the conditions of war in the country and the very precarious situation in BH, we believe that in all the regions and in the entire BH, detailed contingency plans" --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We've got the normal problem, Your Honour. The witness is looking for the passage. He's therefore not concentrating on what's being put to him. What's being put to him he cannot find because it's not there --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, can I have your attention for just a moment. I thought the Court's explanation would have been understood, but if I could just explain it quickly again. The passage I'm citing now is a comment by Mr. Miskin before you spoke at the session. It has not been duplicated in the B/C/S, and so it's no wonder you're unable to find it. My apologies for that. I'm going to try to read it slowly so that you can hear it. If there's any particular reason why you would want to see it in the writing in the B/C/S, you're more than free to let us know and we can do so. Thereafter, I'll be turning my attention --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So although I started it a number of times, I'll attempt to read it through now. "Given the conditions of war in the country and the very precarious situation in BH, we believe that in all the regions and in the entire BH, detailed contingency plans should be elaborated in the event the Serbian people has to defend itself against various enemies." Let me move directly now, Mr. Kapetina, to your own remarks which are found at pages 57 through 60 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And 98 to 102 of the B/C/S, which you should have in front of you, Mr. Kapetina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We see Mr. Kapetina starts speaking on page 58. So someone may have worked from a different copy. I think we will find our way. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kapetina is -- you begin by noting that the -- you have -- you and the ministry of national defence have drafted a paper entitled "organisational and functional principles of the system of defence in BH. Naturally, from the aspect of the interests of the Serbian people and tasks in terms of decentralisation of relations in this field." And in the interest of time, let me attempt to focus your attention on two particular aspects of this without necessarily quoting them directly, since you have them in front of you. You propose two solutions, it seems, in your comments. After explaining how in your view the Muslims are planning for a sovereign state with all the attributes of statehood and sovereignty. For that you say: "We have proposed two solutions. The first in the event that a sovereign BH is indeed created," and in that case you explain autonomous regions would be formed to protect the interests of the Serbian people, and for that variant you've devised the establishment of an ectogenous, what I understand indigenous system of defence at the level of the autonomous regions. That's at page 58 of the English. I'll let the excerpt speak for itself. And the second model proposed by you is in the event that Bosnia and Herzegovina remains within a federal state, and in that case you note: "We insist on an even stronger centralisation of the system of defence and don't want dual armed forces." Now, Mr. Kapetina, although we went through a lot of discussion about tasks that -- the question of whether or not you were assigned tasks and performed tasks, isn't this an example of precisely that, that it doesn't leave any doubt about whether or not you received that assignment and whether or not you performed it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not receive tasks and I didn't carry tasks out. This is a task of the vice-premier, and it wasn't only I myself who worked on this concept but a group in the Ministry of Defence. So the vice-premier, Miodrag Simovic, I don't know whether already at that time he was president of the ministerial council, I'm not sure whether he was or not, but we received a task from the vice-premier, so these were just possible variations. Of course my views on the ministry and the problems in the system of defence and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Conducted, as I believe you indicated in the first sentence of your remarks: "naturally from the aspects of the interests of the Serbian people" --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That's the kind of task we were issued from the vice-premier. Do you mean to say that the Serbian people did not exist in Bosnia and Herzegovina and that it wasn't a constituent peoples? Did I perhaps say that I wasn't a Serb, that I denied being a Serb here?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Kapetina. I'd like you to turn next to tab 9, which is a previously marked exhibit as P64, P65; Treanor, tab 78. That's the minutes of the first meeting of the ministerial council of the Serbian people. You may recall Mr. Miskin's call at the third session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly for the establishment of a council of ministers to implement the tasks outlined by the groups that were reporting at that session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly. And in particular, in his concern, to implement regionalisation. This is the first meeting of the ministerial council, and if I can ask you to turn your attention to the conclusions found at page 3 of the English, and specifically to conclusion number 3 which states: "The issues regarding cooperation with JNA organs and commands should be treated in the rules of procedure of the ministerial council. Ljubisav Terzic, Dragan Mirkovic, and Dragan Kapetina are entrusted with this task." Mr. Kapetina, isn't this yet another example of you being tasked with responsibilities in connection with pursuing the SDS programme or by SDS high-ranking officials and, in this case in particular, in connection with coordination and cooperation with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I'm concerned, this isn't an SDS organ. The ministerial council is a group of ministers from the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and we -- Terzic, myself, and Dragan Mirkovic were tasked and we were assistants in the Ministry of Defence. So as far as I'm concerned, this is a state task.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, we're almost out of time, so let me ask you one or two quick questions. Are you suggesting that you are not aware now and were not aware then that the ministerial council was composed of members of the government who were SDS members or representatives or who were affiliated with SDS in contrast to a multi-ethnic body?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that I should not have recognised the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina composed of cadres of the SDS, SDA, and HDZ? Is that what you want me to do? I knew that it was composed of those three parties and the representatives of those three ethnic groups; of course I knew that. As far as I was concerned, it was the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's quite the contrary, Mr. Kapetina. This meeting of the ministerial council, this first meeting of the ministerial council on July 11th [sic] is the ministerial council of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is not a multi-party, multi-ethnic body, is it, or was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned it is not a party body. As far as I am concerned, the ministers in the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina are part of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetina, we're out of time for the day, but I submit to you that you knew precisely what the nature of these questions were. In fact, His Honour Judge Orie clarified it for you, and that you have attempted purposefully to evade your work on behalf of these Serbian bodies until confronted with them, and when confronted them, attempt to recharacterise the questions. Isn't that, in fact, what's happening here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KAPETINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, I take it that you misspoke when you said "the first meeting on the 11th of July," where it gives the 11th of January as the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we finish, Mr. Kapetina, I specifically asked you about ever receiving tasks of the SDS. I also spoke about individuals who held -- SDS members who held high positions. And I do not know whether there's any confusion in this respect, but you said: Should I not have recognised the government in Bosnia and Herzegovina? The documents you were confronted with, the minutes of this first meeting of ministerial council, is not of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a whole. Is there any misunderstanding about that? Or same for the 11th of December, third session of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina. These were Serb organs or Serb institutions, and not anymore of the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Or do I not understand the meaning of these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my answers I stated quite categorically that I had never received a task from the functionaries of the Serbian Democratic Party, organs of the Serbian Democratic Party in 1991, and that's the truth. And I state that quite categorically, as far as I'm concerned, the vice-premier of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or any minister for that matter, not only functionaries of the Serbian Democratic Party, but the government itself. Now I'm asking the question: Are the rest of the members of the government the legitimate members of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina? And why they would be legitimate. The constitution and the law is being implemented now, but when I insisted it was not being implemented. So that's that selective approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just re-read your answer. So let's -- let me try to understand you. Is it your position that you say since Mr. Simovic was the vice-premier of Bosnia and Herzegovina, whatever --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Government --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whatever -- yes, vice-premier of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that whatever tasks I received, I received them from a member of the legitimate government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. At the same time - and that seems to be the issue Mr. Tieger is raising - is that tasking you with these kind of matters is at least discussed in organs that were at that time predominantly, if I may say so, Serb organs and not organs created by the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So we now see Mr. Simovic appearing in two different contexts, two different environments; one being -- I would say constitutionally BiH, and the other one, to say at least, not provided for in the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina but predominantly Serb. Do I understand your testimony well that you say: Well, whatever task I got, I always got it from someone who held an official constitutional position in BiH, and it's of no importance that these tasks and the performance of these tasks were discussed in totally different contexts, predominantly Serb contexts, as well? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. I didn't know about the conversations between Simovic and Karadzic, and I wasn't interested in that or any other conversation. I received this task. I didn't receive any particular tasks that year anyway, but I received that task from the vice-premier, Miodrag Simovic. And I would just like to make one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I may ask one additional question before you add something to that. You were working in the Ministry of Defence, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Isn't it true that civil servants in a Ministry of Defence receive their tasks usually from their superiors in that same ministry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you explain how the vice-premier gave you tasks? Directly, indirectly, through your minister? I do not know. Could you please explain this for us, and then -- this is for the interpreters, then I will stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that yesterday I said in answer to questions by the Defence, that Minister Doko himself called vice-premier Simovic and told him: Kapetina is available for you as of today. He will not be receiving tasks from me. If I recall, I think that that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what you said. So you said you received these instructions by the vice-premier on the basis of Mr. Doko having told him that you were available for him. Yes. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's then finish for the day, and that at least clarifies a few matters. We'd like to see you back tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, and we hope then to finish tomorrow in the afternoon. May I again instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony and -- already given or testimony still to be given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to make one remark. These comments are very detailed. I cannot follow such complicated details or subjective assessments. It's difficult to tell what the actual questions are. Perhaps the comments could be cut short, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll try to do the same as what we expect you to do, is to be as much focussing on what's the core of the question, and then you focus on the core of the answer to that question. We stand adjourned until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, with, again, the appreciation of the Chamber for the interpreters and technicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 19th day of January, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.11 p.m.,
